findings.label: Paid During Active Breaches
findings.detail: 4 suppliers received payments while in breach of Companies Act — including 0 critical and 0 high severity. Temporally verified against payment dates.

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 406 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 2393 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: Adult Services and Wellbeing-Adult Health & Social Care spent 8.5x their monthly average in March (£58.5M above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Reen Technologies Ltd (2.0 day avg, 13 payments, £12.8K)

findings.label: Benford's Law Anomaly
findings.detail: Significant deviation from Benford's Law (p < 0.001). Digit 1 deviates 9.5% from expected distribution across 362,079 transactions. Note: with 362,079 transactions, chi-squared tests are highly sensitive — the 9.5% max digit deviation is the more practical measure of anomaly.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 362,079+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (9.5%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 407,358 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 7 deviates 7.47% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=407,358.

key_findings.title: 10 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Andrew Greenwood Electrical Ltd — every 3.7 days (4955 payments, £1.9M)

key_findings.title: REED SPECIALIST RECRUITMENT LTD: 13318 transactions totalling £13.4M
key_findings.description: Averaging £1.0K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier
